clue.text: Display in this paper a meteorological event

indicators.note: in places the display word inside the paper's nickname

parts.note: The Thunderer is the old nickname of The Times, the paper printing the clue
to display is to show

explanation.surface: The newspaper is putting on a show about the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times was long nicknamed The Thunderer, so 'this paper' points to that name; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden storm of rain with thunder is a weather phenomenon.

clue.text: In discussion on art, silent? On the contrary

parts.note: people in discussion are talking
a painting is a work of art, a picture

explanation.surface: A remark about art debates whether a work can be silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the reverse of a silent film: an early film with sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A silent film's opposite is a film with a soundtrack, the early 'talkie'.

clue.text: Female in group is inadequate

indicators.note: in puts the female letter inside the group word

parts.note: a unit is a group, as in a military unit

explanation.surface: A woman in the team is not up to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not fit for a role is not good enough, lacking in capacity.

clue.text: To ruin a single farm building is 'not the best policy

parts.note: to dish someone's chances is to ruin them
a single thing is one
a sty is a pig's shed on a farm

explanation.surface: Wrecking a lone barn is said to be a poor way to behave.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'honesty is the best policy'; its opposite is not the best policy.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says honesty is the best policy, so its opposite, lying, is not.

clue.text: Set free after rising or subjected to abuse

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to deliver is to set free, as from captivity

explanation.surface: A prisoner either freed after an uprising or badly treated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reviled is to be abused verbally, insulted and denounced.

clue.text: Sort of car it's difficult to beat

explanation.surface: A car advertised as unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as 'hard to top', i.e. difficult to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with a rigid roof is one type; and something hard to top is hard to better.

clue.text: Express for news

explanation.definitionFit: To put something into words is to phrase it; and a word from someone can mean tidings or a message.

clue.text: Part of film about Bolshevik leader; hero in revolt

indicators.note: about means the film part goes round the leader's letter

parts.note: a reel is a section of a film

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a lion is a brave person, a hero

explanation.surface: A segment of a movie about Lenin shows a hero in an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising against authority is a revolt.

clue.text: Sounds like supporter and girl in story of childhood

indicators.note: Sounds like says the supporter word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a sider is one who takes a side, a supporter
with means together with, and
Rosie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A fan and a girl appear in a tale of growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurie Lee's memoir of a Cotswold childhood; CIDER is heard as SIDER, one who sides with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurie Lee's 1959 memoir describes his boyhood in a Gloucestershire village.

clue.text: Doctor flies to state as helper in emergency

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A physician flies off to a US state to help in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rescues people from danger is a rescuer in a crisis.

clue.text: Religious leader — one who is inconclusive

indicators.note: inconclusive means the word loses its conclusion, its final letter

parts.note: a rabbit is one who rabbits on, a chatterer

explanation.surface: A clergyman described as someone who never reaches a conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: A chatterer who rabbits on is a RABBIT; 'inconclusive' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish teacher and spiritual head of a congregation.

clue.text: Some ain't round for the opening …

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some boxers are not around for the first round.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction is the opening section of a piece of music or writing.

clue.text: … and others come back tardily

indicators.note: come back means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: et al. is Latin for and others

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the rest return behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues from 11 across, but this clue stands alone: ET AL reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving after the expected time is arriving behind schedule.

clue.text: Material for sculptor, say, or painter

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a sculptor models in clay

explanation.surface: A list of art materials and artists.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Klee, the Swiss-German painter, whose name is pronounced like CLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-born modernist artist.

clue.text: Consider for some purpose

explanation.definitionFit: To ponder something carefully; and intentional, done with an aim in mind.

clue.text: Gotterdammerung bringing unexpected plus

explanation.surface: Wagner's opera bringing a welcome surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's Götterdämmerung means 'Twilight of the Gods', read here as the gods' end.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's title means the twilight of the deities; a stroke of unexpected luck is a blessing.

clue.text: Failed 'attempt to impress that produces no good report

definitions.text: Failed 'attempt to impress that produces no good report

parts.words: Failed 'attempt to impress that produces no good report
parts.note: a firework that fizzles out gives no loud bang, the report; figuratively a flop

explanation.surface: A show-off's effort earns no praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a review, but it is the bang of a firework.
explanation.definitionFit: A firework that fails to go off is a figurative term for an anticlimax.

clue.text: Take early look at page in front of critical publication

indicators.note: in front of places the page letter before the publication

parts.note: a review is a magazine of criticism

explanation.surface: Glance at a page ahead of a critics' magazine coming out.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a film or play before general release is to view it in advance.

clue.text: It means disruption for the occupants

indicators.note: disruption means the letters of these words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Something causes chaos for the residents.
explanation.definitionFit: People held in a prison or hospital are its residents.

clue.text: Enlarged circle, with lines -in all directions

indicators.note: in puts the circle and lines inside the compass letters

parts.note: south, west, east and north are all four compass directions
O is a circle
L is line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A ring with lines radiating every way has grown bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points S, W, E, N go round O and LL, giving SW-OLL-EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something puffed up is swelled in size.

clue.text: It's designed to contain shock in earth's quaking

indicators.note: quaking earth shakes, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: Something is built to absorb the jolt of an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' means a shock of hair, not a seismic jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh worn to keep a mass of hair in place.

clue.text: Henry and I save swimmer in Atlantic

parts.note: Hal is a short form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
but means save, except

explanation.surface: A man and his friend rescue someone swimming in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flatfish found in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Mission one's taken to when rebuked

explanation.surface: An errand someone is sent on after a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part plays on the idiom 'taken to task', meaning rebuked.
explanation.definitionFit: An assigned job or mission; and the idiom 'take to task' means to scold.

clue.text: Vessel in nautical front line

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A ship sits in the front line at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship but means a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A round dish is a container, a vessel for food.

clue.text: Novel set in royal town

indicators.note: set in means the novel's title is placed inside the royal letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher
She is H. Rider Haggard's novel

explanation.surface: A book whose action takes place in a town with royal links.
explanation.walkthrough: ESHER is a commuter town in Surrey, south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Esher is a Surrey settlement near London.

clue.text: Haircut getting a female upset 'in Mediterranean port

indicators.note: cut means the word is clipped of its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read upwards

explanation.surface: A woman upset by her haircut at a seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is Israel's chief harbour city.

clue.text: Hail, at sea, a sailing vessel

parts.note: a hoy is a small coasting sailing boat

explanation.surface: A greeting called out to a passing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailor's call used to greet a ship.

clue.text: Below par for part of the golf course

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling unwell is feeling poorly; and the long grass beside a golf fairway.

clue.text: Overlapping signs in places for readers

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: overlapping means the shared letter of the two signs is used once

parts.note: Aries is another zodiac sign

explanation.surface: Star signs appearing in reading rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: LIBRA and ARIES overlap on their shared A, giving LIBR-A-RIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lending institutions where people go to read books.

clue.text: Like outcasts, not understood by white people?

explanation.surface: Social outcasts misunderstood by the establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads it literally: beyond the reach of pale people.
explanation.definitionFit: Outside the bounds of acceptable behaviour; and literally past pale-skinned people's grasp.
